one_liner: Browser FLV player that soft-decodes H.264/H.265 in WebAssembly/asm.js; claims lower CPU than FFmpeg-based wasm players.
what_it_does: A JavaScript player for HTTP-FLV (live and on-demand) that demuxes FLV and decodes H.264 or H.265 in a Web Worker running Emscripten-compiled C/C++, then draws YUV frames with WebGL and plays AAC through Web Audio. It exists to get inline, autoplaying video inside Chinese mobile browsers and the WeChat WebView, which restrict the HTML5 video element. The API is a player object (new WXInlinePlayer({url, $container, ...}) with play/pause/resume/stop/volume/mute/destroy and events such as playing, buffering and performance), not a drop-in decoder library. Three prebuilt decoder bundles are chosen at init: baseline (TinyH264, Baseline profile only), all (OpenH264, Baseline/Main/High) and h265 (libde265).
how_it_is_fast: Instead of a slimmed FFmpeg build (the README cites about 2 MB, 600 KB gzipped), it links small single-purpose decoders (TinyH264 about 180 KB, OpenH264 about 260 KB, libde265 about 210 KB gzipped) behind its own C++ FLV demuxer, built with Emscripten -O3, Closure and --llvm-lto 3. The H.265 bundle's speed gain comes mainly from doing less work: lib/codec/src/codec/codec.h sets DE265_DECODER_PARAM_DISABLE_DEBLOCKING and DE265_DECODER_PARAM_DISABLE_SAO to true, so both HEVC in-loop filters are skipped. Rendering uses WebGL YUV-to-RGB on the main thread while decoding stays in a worker.
when_to_use: Inline or autoplaying H.264 FLV clips in the WeChat WebView or other mobile browsers that hijack the native video element (ad, marketing or animation clips).
Low-latency HTTP-FLV live streams at modest settings; the README reports smooth playback of 1280x720, 1024 kbps, 24 fps on mid- to high-end phones and 1-2 s lower latency than MSE-based video.
Pages that are sensitive to decoder download size and only need Baseline-profile H.264 (the TinyH264 bundle).
As reference code for wiring an Emscripten-built decoder, a C++ FLV demuxer and a WebGL YUV renderer together.
when_not_to_use: When picture fidelity matters for H.265: with deblocking and SAO disabled the decoder is not conforming, and because both are in-loop filters the errors propagate through inter-predicted frames until the next random-access picture.

Untrusted or malformed FLV input: the demuxer does not validate NAL length fields, and open issue #118 (June 2026) reports a reproducible memory-safety bug in FLV video-tag parsing with no maintainer reply.
10-bit (Main10) HEVC or non-4:2:0 content: the H.265 output path sizes and copies frames as 8-bit 4:2:0.
Projects that need an OSI licence: the code is under the draft 'Anti 996' License 1.0 (package.json still says ISC).
Anything needing seek, MP4/HLS/DASH containers or active maintenance: seek is a stub (try2seek returns 0), the roadmap items after V1.4 never shipped, and the last commit was 2022-03-26.

integration.dependencies: Bundled third-party decoders (OpenH264, TinyH264, libde265) compiled to wasm/asm.js; JS deps eventemitter3, buffer, mobile-detect, promise-polyfill; building needs parcel, Emscripten 1.38.45 exactly, CMake 3.16+ and make on a Unix host
integration.min_toolchain: Emscripten 1.38.45 (README warns other versions give wasm32 errors), C++11, CMake 3.16+
integration.platforms: Browsers with Worker, fetch, ReadableStream, Web Audio, AAC support and WebGL (falls back to asm.js without WebAssembly); README lists Android 5+, iOS 10+, Chrome 25+, Firefox 57+, Edge 15+, Safari 10.1+; UC and Quark browsers explicitly refused
integration.thread_safety: Not documented; the wasm module holds one global Codec instance (main.cpp), so each player needs its own worker

gotchas: The H.265 build turns off both deblocking and SAO (codec.h: DE265_DECODER_PARAM_DISABLE_DEBLOCKING and DE265_DECODER_PARAM_DISABLE_SAO set true) and does not suppress faulty pictures; the README only says 'reduced deblock'. The 30% H.265 advantage over FFmpeg-based players therefore compares unequal work: FFmpeg's HEVC decoder runs both in-loop filters.

FLV/NAL parsing trusts length fields: Buffer::slice has no bounds check, read_uint8 asserts offset <= length (off by one), and the H.265 path slices each NAL by a 32-bit length read from the stream; issues #48 and #84 report 'memory access out of bounds' on real HTTP-FLV streams and #118 reports a sanitizer-reproducible memory-safety bug.

H.265 frames are copied as width*height*3/2 bytes of 8-bit 4:2:0 and tagged with the FLV tag timestamp of the packet that released them, not the picture's own presentation time, so reordered or high-bit-depth streams can show wrong timing or garbage.
Production builds keep Emscripten ASSERTIONS=1, and H.265 in FLV relies on the Kingsoft (ksvc) FLV extension, so standard FFmpeg cannot mux it without the ksvc patch.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Among the catalogued wasm media entries, TurboRes targets ProRes decoding and Pare targets encoding against ffmpeg.wasm; pick WXInlinePlayer only when the job is playing H.264/H.265 FLV (especially live HTTP-FLV) inline inside WeChat or similar WebViews.
verified_claims_summary: First-party only: a README screenshot (images/benchmark.png) of H.265 FLV playback on the developer's own machine shows mean CPU 64% and memory 162 MB versus 91-102% and 174-202 MB for WASMVideoPlayer and the Taobao and Huajiao FFmpeg-based players, with clip, resolution, browser and hardware unstated and no benchmark code. The code shows the H.265 decoder skips deblocking and SAO, so the gain is partly from producing a lower-quality, non-conforming picture rather than from a faster equivalent decoder.
status_note: Abandoned since 2022-03-26 (231 commits, 1.5k stars, 14 open issues including an unanswered memory-safety report) and under the non-OSI draft Anti-996 licence, so reference only; pin Emscripten 1.38.45 if you must rebuild it.
